title: Senior asks: a user saves the text "Äpfel" with write on a .json file. What is in the file?
explain: JsonFileActions::write() does not use JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE, so json_encode() writes non-ASCII letters as \u escapes. The file is still valid JSON and read() gives "Äpfel" back. But people who open the file see codes. Add the flag if humans read the files.

title: Senior asks: a CSV row has the fruit "Apple, red" (with a comma). What does write() save?
explain: fputcsv() puts quotes around a value that has the separator, a quote or a new line. So the file keeps two columns, and read() with READ_CSV gets "Apple, red" back. Writing CSV by hand with implode(',') would break this row into three columns.

title: Senior asks: a.json has one object with a name and a list of 3 items. What does read() tell the user?
explain: count() only counts the top level. The object has two keys, name and items, so the message says 2 records. The 3 items inside are not counted. The message is made for a list of rows, so for an object it is misleading. You could say 'keys' or check array_is_list().

title: Senior asks: you move the project to full Symfony. What replaces ACTION_METHODS and the match in handle()?
options: Route attributes like #[Route('/files/{name}', methods: ['DELETE'])] on controller methods
A bigger switch with more cases in index.php
explain: The Symfony router maps URL and HTTP method to one controller method. Wrong method gives 405 and unknown path gives 404 without your code. So ACTION_METHODS, checkAction() and match disappear. The method list now lives in one place: the attribute.

title: An API returns a filtered list. What does this print?
explain: array_filter() removes 0 and keeps the old keys 0 and 2. A PHP array with keys that are not 0,1,2... in order becomes a JSON object. The front end expects a list and gets an object. Use array_values(array_filter($list)) to get [5,7].

title: A static counter and a child class. What does this print?
explain: A child class does not get its own copy of a static property. A::$n and B::$n are the same variable, so two calls give 2 for both. To give B its own counter, declare public static int $n = 0; again inside B. Static state is shared: be careful with it.

title: You want to know if your installed packages have known security problems. Which command?
explain: composer audit checks the packages in composer.lock against a list of known security advisories. validate checks the composer.json file. outdated only shows newer versions, not security. dump-autoload rebuilds the class map. Run audit in CI so a bad package fails the build.

title: A fetch() gets the answer 404. What does Node print?
explain: fetch() only rejects on network errors, like no connection. A 404 or 500 answer is a normal result, so .then() runs and r.ok is false. Always check r.ok (or r.status) yourself. Unlike jQuery $.ajax, where the error callback runs for 404.
